fields.label: L1 One-Line Flash Anchor
fields.value: Presented as translations of ancient Gaelic material; authenticity became controversial.

fields.label: 2-Minute Simple Biography
fields.value: James Macpherson was a Scottish poet who claimed to translate ancient poems. He was born at Ruthven, in Inverness, on 27 October 1736. He died at Belville, in Inverness, on 17 February 1796. He said a third century bard named Ossian wrote the poems.

fields.label: Why Important for UGC NET
fields.value: UGC NET asks Macpherson in Unit 2 (Poetry) for the Ossian poems. Questions test 1760, the Fingal date, and Temora in 1763. They also ask about the forgery charge (the claim that the ancient poems were made up).

fields.label: Memory Tip & Exam Traps
fields.value: Ossian: Fragments 1760, Fingal issued 1761 with a 1762 title page, Temora 1763. | Presented as translations of ancient Gaelic material; authenticity became controversial.

fields.value: Anna Laetitia Barbauld was an English poet, essayist, and editor. She was born Anna Laetitia Aikin at Kibworth Harcourt on 20 June 1743. She died at Stoke Newington on 9 March 1825. She grew up among Dissenters (Protestants outside the Church of England) and later edited a huge set of novels.

fields.label: Why Important for UGC NET
fields.value: UGC NET may ask Barbauld in Unit 2 (Poetry) and also in Unit 3 because she edited novels. Match Poems with 1773 and Eighteen Hundred and Eleven with publication in 1812. The British Novelists (1810) is her edition, not a novel she wrote.

fields.value: Charlotte Smith

fields.label: L1 One-Line Flash Anchor

fields.label: 2-Minute Simple Biography
fields.value: Charlotte Smith was an English poet and novelist of the early Romantic age. She was born in 1749 and died in 1806. A very young marriage and money troubles pushed her to write for her children. Her mournful sonnets (poems of 14 lines) helped revive that form in English.

fields.label: Why Important for UGC NET
fields.value: UGC NET asks her under Unit 2 (Poetry) for the sonnet revival and poem dates. Unit 3 (Fiction) fits her novels, which are separate from these three poems. Coleridge credited her and William Lisle Bowles with bringing the sonnet back.

fields.label: Memory Tip & Exam Traps
fields.value: Sonnets in 1784, The Emigrants in 1793, and Beachy Head in 1807. | Beachy Head appeared posthumously.

fields.value: William Wordsworth was a major English Romantic poet. He was born in Cockermouth in 1770 and died in 1850. With Samuel Taylor Coleridge, he helped start the English Romantic movement. He served as the Poet Laureate of the United Kingdom from 1843 until his death.

fields.label: Why Important for UGC NET

fields.value: Dorothy Wordsworth was an English journal writer of the Romantic age. She was born in 1771 at Cockermouth and died in 1855 at Rydal Mount. She was the sister and close companion of the poet William Wordsworth. Her nature notes helped shape several of his poems.

fields.label: 2-Minute Simple Biography
fields.value: Raja Rammohun Roy was a Bengali religious and social reformer. He was born in 1772 at Radhanagar and died in 1833 at Bristol in England. He is often called a father of modern India. He argued for worship of one God, and he fought sati (the burning of a widow on her husband's fire).

fields.value: UGC NET asks Roy under Unit 4 (non fictional prose). Questions test the 1820 Precepts of Jesus and the Upanishad tracts. Upanishads are old Hindu texts on the one supreme reality. Do not treat the Upanishad entry as one single book.

fields.value: Thomas Moore was an Irish poet, songwriter, and biographer. He was born in Dublin in 1779 and died in England in 1852. He was a Catholic, and his songs spoke for Ireland. He was a close friend of Lord Byron.
